{
  "project_id": "P-MEX-SustainableValueChains",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Low market uptake of the new Sustainability‑Linked Loan (SLL) and Green Loan (GL) products may limit financing volumes.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement step‑down pricing incentives, conduct targeted outreach to mid‑caps and SMEs, and monitor uptake to adjust incentives quickly.",
      "evidence": "Market for sustainable finance instruments remains nascent and concentrated among large corporations (Section B.7)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Credit risk of SME and mid‑cap borrowers due to weak collateral and high information asymmetry.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Require minimum co‑financing, use independent validation of sustainability plans, and apply risk‑adjusted pricing margins.",
      "evidence": "Limited collateral recovery, information asymmetries, and short‑term funding structures constrain SME financing (Section B.13‑B.15)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Insufficient Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) capacity may delay loan approvals and affect ESG compliance.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide dedicated MRV training to PFIs and BEs, fund initial MRV costs, and develop standardized digital tools.",
      "evidence": "Limited availability of credible MRV systems constrains lenders’ capacity (Section B.15)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Risk of greenwashing if sustainability plans are not rigorously validated.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Mandate ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification by independent entities for all SLL/GL projects.",
      "evidence": "To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets will be subject to ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification (Section D.1a)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Women‑owned firms may be under‑represented among loan beneficiaries, limiting gender impact goals.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set explicit women‑inclusive eligibility criteria, track gender metrics, and run targeted outreach campaigns.",
      "evidence": "Women‑owned firms have lower access to formal financing (Section B.20‑B.21)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Physical climate risks (heatwaves, floods) could impair beneficiary operations and loan repayment.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Integrate climate‑risk assessments into loan underwriting and promote resilience‑enhancing technologies.",
      "evidence": "Extreme weather raises loan delinquency rates among Mexican firms (Section B.19)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Delay in adopting the Project Operations Manual and Sustainable Finance Framework could postpone disbursements.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set interim milestones, monitor adoption progress, and provide technical assistance to expedite approvals.",
      "evidence": "Effectiveness requires adoption of the POM and Sustainable Finance Framework (Conditions section)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Participating Financial Institutions (PFIs) may lack expertise to appraise and monitor green loans.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Deliver capacity‑building TA to PFIs on green‑loan underwriting, risk assessment, and monitoring tools.",
      "evidence": "Mexican financial institutions are limited in capacity to design, originate, appraise and monitor green loans (Section B.15)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Non‑compliance with environmental and social standards could trigger legal or reputational penalties.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Embed strict ESMS clauses in loan agreements, conduct bi‑annual E&S reporting, and audit high‑risk borrowers.",
      "evidence": "E&S risk is Substantial; compliance clauses will be incorporated into loan agreements (Section C.3)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Currency fluctuations may affect the real cost of MXN‑denominated loans for borrowers and NAFIN.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "NAFIN to hedge FX exposure via swaps and monitor exchange‑rate movements regularly.",
      "evidence": "NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s currency swap market (Section D.31)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Strict eligibility and retroactive‑financing limits could cause cash‑flow gaps for early‑stage projects.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide clear guidance on eligible pre‑signature expenditures and allow timely advance requests within the $40 M cap.",
      "evidence": "Withdrawals prior to Signature Date limited to $40 M for eligible expenditures (Disbursement section)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Reliance on legacy financial systems may cause reporting delays and errors.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement interim data‑reconciliation procedures, conduct regular internal audits, and plan gradual digitalization.",
      "evidence": "Residual FM risk moderate due to reliance on legacy information systems (Section B.54)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Grievance Redress Service may be under‑utilized, leading to unresolved stakeholder complaints.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Promote the GRS through the Stakeholder Engagement Plan, set response‑time targets, and monitor complaint logs.",
      "evidence": "SEP includes a Grievance Redress Mechanism to receive and address Project‑related complaints (Section C.60)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Targeted private capital mobilization of US$89 M may not be achieved, limiting leverage effect.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Activate co‑financing requirements, engage anchor companies early, and showcase pilot successes to attract investors.",
      "evidence": "Project will help mobilize an estimated US$89 M in private capital (Section D.28)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Beneficiary firms may lack technical capacity to implement renewable or energy‑efficiency technologies.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide feasibility studies, technical assistance, and subsidized MRV support for high‑impact technologies.",
      "evidence": "Most firms lack capacity to measure emissions, implement energy‑use systems, or comply with reporting frameworks (Section B.15‑B.16)."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Low market uptake of the new Sustainability‑Linked Loan (SLL) and Green Loan (GL) products may limit financing volumes.
risks.mitigation: Implement step‑down pricing incentives, conduct targeted outreach to mid‑caps and SMEs, and monitor uptake to adjust incentives quickly.
risks.evidence: Market for sustainable finance instruments remains nascent and concentrated among large corporations (Section B.7).

risks.description: Credit risk of SME and mid‑cap borrowers due to weak collateral and high information asymmetry.
risks.mitigation: Require minimum co‑financing, use independent validation of sustainability plans, and apply risk‑adjusted pricing margins.
risks.evidence: Limited collateral recovery, information asymmetries, and short‑term funding structures constrain SME financing (Section B.13‑B.15).

risks.description: Insufficient Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) capacity may delay loan approvals and affect ESG compliance.
risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated MRV training to PFIs and BEs, fund initial MRV costs, and develop standardized digital tools.
risks.evidence: Limited availability of credible MRV systems constrains lenders’ capacity (Section B.15).

risks.description: Risk of greenwashing if sustainability plans are not rigorously validated.
risks.mitigation: Mandate ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification by independent entities for all SLL/GL projects.
risks.evidence: To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets will be subject to ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification (Section D.1a).

risks.description: Women‑owned firms may be under‑represented among loan beneficiaries, limiting gender impact goals.
risks.mitigation: Set explicit women‑inclusive eligibility criteria, track gender metrics, and run targeted outreach campaigns.
risks.evidence: Women‑owned firms have lower access to formal financing (Section B.20‑B.21).

risks.description: Physical climate risks (heatwaves, floods) could impair beneficiary operations and loan repayment.
risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑risk assessments into loan underwriting and promote resilience‑enhancing technologies.
risks.evidence: Extreme weather raises loan delinquency rates among Mexican firms (Section B.19).

risks.description: Delay in adopting the Project Operations Manual and Sustainable Finance Framework could postpone disbursements.
risks.mitigation: Set interim milestones, monitor adoption progress, and provide technical assistance to expedite approvals.
risks.evidence: Effectiveness requires adoption of the POM and Sustainable Finance Framework (Conditions section).

risks.description: Participating Financial Institutions (PFIs) may lack expertise to appraise and monitor green loans.
risks.mitigation: Deliver capacity‑building TA to PFIs on green‑loan underwriting, risk assessment, and monitoring tools.
risks.evidence: Mexican financial institutions are limited in capacity to design, originate, appraise and monitor green loans (Section B.15).

risks.description: Non‑compliance with environmental and social standards could trigger legal or reputational penalties.
risks.mitigation: Embed strict ESMS clauses in loan agreements, conduct bi‑annual E&S reporting, and audit high‑risk borrowers.
risks.evidence: E&S risk is Substantial; compliance clauses will be incorporated into loan agreements (Section C.3).

risks.description: Currency fluctuations may affect the real cost of MXN‑denominated loans for borrowers and NAFIN.
risks.mitigation: NAFIN to hedge FX exposure via swaps and monitor exchange‑rate movements regularly.
risks.evidence: NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s currency swap market (Section D.31).

risks.description: Strict eligibility and retroactive‑financing limits could cause cash‑flow gaps for early‑stage projects.
risks.mitigation: Provide clear guidance on eligible pre‑signature expenditures and allow timely advance requests within the $40 M cap.
risks.evidence: Withdrawals prior to Signature Date limited to $40 M for eligible expenditures (Disbursement section).

risks.description: Reliance on legacy financial systems may cause reporting delays and errors.
risks.mitigation: Implement interim data‑reconciliation procedures, conduct regular internal audits, and plan gradual digitalization.
risks.evidence: Residual FM risk moderate due to reliance on legacy information systems (Section B.54).

risks.description: Grievance Redress Service may be under‑utilized, leading to unresolved stakeholder complaints.
risks.mitigation: Promote the GRS through the Stakeholder Engagement Plan, set response‑time targets, and monitor complaint logs.
risks.evidence: SEP includes a Grievance Redress Mechanism to receive and address Project‑related complaints (Section C.60).

risks.description: Targeted private capital mobilization of US$89 M may not be achieved, limiting leverage effect.
risks.mitigation: Activate co‑financing requirements, engage anchor companies early, and showcase pilot successes to attract investors.
risks.evidence: Project will help mobilize an estimated US$89 M in private capital (Section D.28).

risks.description: Beneficiary firms may lack technical capacity to implement renewable or energy‑efficiency technologies.
risks.mitigation: Provide feasibility studies, technical assistance, and subsidized MRV support for high‑impact technologies.
risks.evidence: Most firms lack capacity to measure emissions, implement energy‑use systems, or comply with reporting frameworks (Section B.15‑B.16).
